note: Every future end-to-end gate for the eight parity capabilities that depend on a REAL external provider (semantic video understanding, transcription, diarization, and rendered-draft multimodal critique against real media). All gates here are pending by design. A gate flips to passed ONLY when its executable end-to-end check actually passes against real output. Nothing here may be marked green while the backing external provider is unverified. The LOCAL, offline product capabilities (the authenticated review/publishing server, local deterministic generation, grant-gated materialization, and the browser editor) are tracked and executable-verified separately in PRODUCT_ACCEPTANCE.json; they are intentionally NOT listed here so this parity manifest cannot be read as claiming external-provider evidence it does not have.

gates.title: Semantic segments from real footage
gates.description: Given a real source clip, the provider returns time-ranged semantic segments whose ranges are within the clip duration, are non-overlapping or explicitly nested, and whose salience ranks a known key moment above filler.

gates.title: Word-level timing accuracy
gates.description: Transcribing a known clip yields words whose start/end times are monotonic, lie within the clip, and align to a reference transcript within a stated tolerance.

gates.title: Speaker diarization
gates.description: A two-speaker clip returns at least two distinct speaker labels and assigns each reference line to the correct speaker within a stated accuracy.

gates.title: Filler, silence, crew-prompt and take marks
gates.description: A clip seeded with fillers, dead silence, an off-camera crew prompt, and a repeated take produces marks that flag each, and groups the repeated take.

gates.title: Frame-anchored critique of the rendered master
gates.description: Given a rendered master with a known defect at a known time, the critique returns a note anchored within tolerance of that time and marks a blocker.

gates.title: Bounded revision loop
gates.description: Revision proposals validate against the edit-plan schema, re-render, and the loop halts at the configured round cap, escalating to a human rather than looping.

gates.title: Offline local discovery
gates.description: Local discovery finds a seeded relevant asset under the asset root with no network access, returning a portable relative reference.

gates.title: Rights-safe results only
gates.description: Every returned candidate carries explicit license id and attribution data; a candidate lacking a permissive license is never returned, and no unlicensed bytes are fetched.

gates.title: Complete distinct hook set
gates.description: Requesting N hook variants returns exactly N distinct variants, each with a renderer-ready plan fragment that validates against the edit-plan schema.

gates.title: Official surface only
gates.description: Hermes connection uses only a configured MCP, API, or plugin endpoint and never reads a private credential store; unauthorized surfaces are refused.

gates.title: Standalone still works without Hermes
gates.description: With Hermes fully absent, the full offline plan-to-master pipeline still runs and passes QA, proving the integration is optional.

gates.title: No apply without approval
gates.description: Applying an unapproved proposal is refused; applying is permitted only with an approval decision and a held code-change grant. No silent self-modification path exists.

gates.title: Reversible with passing tests
gates.description: An applied proposal ships with tests that pass, and its rollback plan restores the prior state verifiably.

gates.title: Frame comments persist
gates.description: A frame comment added at a time is stored against the correct version and retrievable with its anchor and resolved state.

gates.title: Approvals gated by role
gates.description: Only an approver or admin role can approve; a viewer or commenter is refused. Approval state is recorded on the version.

gates.title: Version comparison
gates.description: Comparing two stored versions returns a truthful diff summary reflecting the real differences between the two masters.

gates.title: Publishing adapter with RBAC and grants
gates.description: Publishing requires an approved version, a publisher/admin role, and held publishing and media-upload grants; without any of these it is refused.
